image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a European fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra) on a textured, light-colored ground surface. The salamander has a glossy black body with distinct, irregular yellow spots and patches. Its skin appears wet and reflective. The head is broad with visible parotoid glands. Forelimbs and hindlimbs are visible, showing short, stout digits. The tail extends towards the background, slightly out of focus. There is some illegible text or watermark in the bottom right corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible, broad, and flattened. The raised areas behind the eyes corresponding to parotoid glands are distinct and match the anatomical description.

The body shape is consistent with a robust, cylindrical salamander morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is vivid black with irregular yellow spots, matching the species' warning pattern perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is smooth, moist, and glandular with a glossy, wet-looking appearance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with four digits on forelimbs and five on hindlimbs; digits are blunt and unwebbed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Visible limbs are short and stout. The front left foot clearly shows four blunt digits. The rear left foot shows multiple digits consistent with five. No webbing is observed.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible extending into the background. It appears laterally compressed and tapers to a rounded tip. Its visible length suggests it is shorter than the body, consistent with the species.
